name: Video Atlas Single-Stream Grid Sync & Viewport Tile Offsetting
description: High-performance video architecture that packs multiple synchronized video clips into a single 5x2 composite video texture (atlas). Eliminates multi-video network thrashing and mobile GPU decoder limits by downloading one shared media stream and offsetting viewports geometrically.
designPhilosophy: Solving the fundamental performance cliff of multi-video web interfaces. Loading 10 separate HTML5 video streams triggers severe mobile hardware decoder limits, battery drain, and network packet contention. The Video Atlas architecture combines all video tiles into a single 5x2 composite video file, downloading one synchronized media stream and using CSS background/transform clipping to display individual tiles.
appropriateUseCases: Video-heavy landing heroes, creator marketplaces, and portfolio lists
E-commerce product grids featuring short video previews on hover
Social media feed mockups and multi-screen interactive installations
implementationApproach: 1. Composite Grid Layout: Pack 10 video clips into a single 16:9 video container formatted as a 5x2 tile matrix (384x540 per tile). 2. Single Shared Video Source: Instantiate video elements pointing to the identical media URI so the browser network cache reuses one HTTP stream. 3. Geometric Tile Offsetting: Inside each clipped card viewport, position the composite video with transform: translate(-col * tileWidth, -row * tileHeight) and scale appropriately. 4. Master Timestamp Synchronization: Synchronize the video instances to identical currentTime values, eliminating audio/frame phase drift. 5. First-Frame Fade-in: Keep poster layer visible until the video's 'canplay' or first frame ready event fires, ensuring seamless presentation without blank frames.
performanceConsiderations: Reduces video network requests by 90% (from 10 requests to 1). Reduces mobile hardware video decoder instances from 10 to 1, preventing out-of-memory crashes on iOS Safari and low-end Android devices.
accessibilityRequirements: All clips are muted by default with no audio track contention. Pauses video playback when the tab is hidden (Document.visibilityState) or when prefers-reduced-motion is enabled, displaying high-resolution static posters instead.
